why: The same turn as ci-100 with the one thing that turn could not have: three datasets that are not the same one. Seeds 1, 2 and 3 record matches 1 to 5000, 2 to 5001 and 3 to 5002 -- match i plays seed s + i -- so ci-100's three datasets shared 4999 matches and the fifth each held out was the next one's training data (journal, 2026-09-16). Every spread this journal has reported was the fit's sensitivity to which fifth was held out, not three draws of the data. Seeds 1, 5001 and 10001 at 5000 matches record 15000 distinct matches. Nothing else moves: lambda 0.9, the ADR 0048 baseline, search-4 as teacher and baseline, explore 0.2. What to read: spread.json against ci-100's widths -- 0.161, 0.339 and 0.064 for the value policy against search-4, Greedy and Random, 0.031 and 0.081 for the clone against Greedy and search-4. An expectation written before the run: the widths should be at least what ci-100 measured, since a fresh draw of the data adds sampling variance on top of the split sensitivity that was already there; a narrower spread would mean the split sensitivity was the larger part and a fresh draw is steadier than a shifted one, which would be worth understanding. Seed 1 is the only one of the three that reproduces ci-100's seed 1 to the digit, and it should. Expect nothing to be committed: at 5000 matches the clone reads at parity with its teacher and the champion. The cost is ci-100's, about an hour and three quarters.
